subject: Latency blip coordination: customer briefing + roadmap ask
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T13:12:00-04:00
Subject: Latency blip detected — BlueWave production (us-east-1)

Quick summary:
- At ~13:05 EDT we saw a transient P99 spike for BlueWave requests hitting the text-generation route in us-east-1. P90 unchanged (~120ms), P99 jumped to ~3.2s for ~8 minutes. Throughput (rps) stayed within SLA.
- Initial signal points at a KV cache miss storm after a small kernel selection change rolled at 12:58 (optimize-kernel-v2).

Immediate mitigation in progress:
1) scaled up the infer-worker pool by +2 nodes (completed 13:09).
2) forced prefix/KV cache refresh for BlueWave tenant (in progress).
3) temporarily pinned BlueWave to kernel v1 while we verify stability (rollback initiated 13:11).

Asks: product (Marissa) and CS (Rishi) — we need a short customer-facing note and decision on whether to offer a credit. Engineering (Hiro) please confirm if kernel selection diff is plausible cause and whether there are any hotfixes beyond rollback.

Logging: I've opened SUP-9876 and attached a short runbook excerpt. Will post a graph shortly.

-Dylan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T13:20:00-04:00
Subject: RE: Latency blip detected — BlueWave production (us-east-1)

Thanks Dylan — good catch and thanks for the quick rollback.

Proposed customer note (one paragraph) below. If product/CS approve, I will send to Natalie and ops@bluewave.com now and offer a 10% credit for the impacted window unless legal flags this. Please review and reply with :+1: to send or suggested edits.

--- draft customer note ---
Natalie — we observed a transient latency increase affecting a subset of BlueWave requests in us-east-1 earlier today. Our SRE team identified the cause as an unintended behavior related to a recent kernel selection optimization; we rolled the change back, scaled additional workers, and forced a cache refresh to restore normal performance. Service is stable now and we are monitoring; we will follow up with a short postmortem and proposed remediation steps. If you prefer, we can offer a one-time service credit for the impacted window. We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.
--- end draft ---

Action items (proposed):
- Dylan: confirm final stabilization and attach latency graph. (assigned)
- Hiro: confirm root cause and whether the kernel selection change requires a patch or configuration guard. ETA 2h. (assigned)
- Marissa: decision on roadmap priority for cache pre-warm / adaptive batching; quick note on whether we should push to P1 for next sprint. (assigned)
- Rishi: send customer note once we have product sign-off; coordinate credit if approved.

I've attached the runbook excerpt and linked the SUP-9876 ticket.

-Rishi
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T13:35:00-04:00
Subject: RE: Latency blip detected — BlueWave production (us-east-1)

Thanks — quick product note: we need a clear distinction between transient ops noise and systemic regressions that require roadmap work. From what's described, two asks for engineering:

1) Confirm whether the kernel selection change can produce cache-thrashing on a per-tenant basis (if yes, that's a safety guard we should add to the rollout system).
2) If the rollback is sufficient short-term, raise a short-term mitigation ticket for cache pre-warming and an infra improvement ticket for "adaptive batching and tenant-aware cache warm-up". I want an ETA for both (hotfix vs. roadmap).

Please include impact estimate on unit-cost and latency if we do pre-warm (ballpark). If this is likely to recur with other kernel improvements, escalate to P1 for next sprint planning.

Also: for customer comms, keep the messaging: "rolled back + scaling + monitoring" and avoid deep technical details unless the customer asks.

-Marissa
Product Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Ramos <natalie@bluewave.com>, BlueWave Ops <ops@bluewave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T14:05:00-04:00
Subject: Update: brief on earlier latency blip (May 8)

Natalie —

I wanted to follow up with a short update on the latency blip you saw earlier today. Our SRE team detected an elevated rate of long-tail latency for a subset of requests and immediately rolled back a recent runtime change, scaled additional workers, and forced a cache refresh for your tenant. Service returned to normal within minutes and we continue to monitor closely.

Next steps: we will share a short postmortem (SUP-9876) with a root cause analysis and remediation steps by EOD tomorrow. As a gesture of goodwill for the disruption, we're prepared to apply a one-time billing credit for the impacted window; let me know if you'd like us to proceed.

Apologies for the interruption — please ping me directly if you need any more detail or a call.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

- Rollback to kernel v1 completed and verified at 13:11.
- Cache refresh completed at 13:15.
- Scaling stabilized latency immediately (graph attached: latency_graph-20270508.png). No additional spikes after 13:19.
- SUP-9876 created and linked. I'll own the postmortem; target is EOD tomorrow.

Follow-ups (owners + ETA):
1) Hiro: confirm whether kernel selector needs a config guard and if a hotfix is needed. ETA 2 hours.
2) Engineering: ticket for cache pre-warm (hotfix) — ETA 3 days to ship a narrow scope fix.
3) Product: review for prioritization of adaptive batching (Marissa) — please advise if you want this P1.
4) CS/Reliability: Rishi to send customer note and credit if approved.

I'll attach the runbook excerpt and a screenshot to the ticket.
